## AZITHROMYCIN FOR PREVENTION OF EXACERBATIONS IN ADVANCED COPD
## Eligibility Criteria:
*Age >40 years
*Clinical diagnosis of COPD (>= 10 pack-years cigarette smoking, a ratio of
postbronchodilator forced expiratory volume in 1 second [FEV1] to forced vital
capacity of <70%, and a postbronchodilator FEV1 of <80% of the predicted value),
*AND*
*Were either using continuous supplemental oxygen or had received systemic
glucocorticoids within the previous year, *OR*
*Had gone to an emergency room or had been hospitalized for an acute
exacerbation of COPD.
## Exclusion criteria:
*Asthma
*People with hearing impairments
*Congestive heart failure
*Resting heart rate > 100 beats per minute
*Use of medications that are associated with torsades de pointes (except for
amiodarone)
*Prolonged QTc interval (>450 msec)
*Use of medications that prolong the QTc interval
Please Click Here for Resource for Drugs that Cause QTc Prolongation
If, after trying all the standard treatments, patients are still having acute
exacerbations of COPD, long-term antibiotic treatment with Azithromycin may be
considered. Note: Guidelines for COPD can be found on the CPRS Tools Menu.
## Select below for Inpatient COPD order sets for comprehensive management:
## Inpatient

Inpatient COPD Exacerbation Orders
If the patient meets the criteria and is willing to have audiometric testing and
an electrocardiogram, please place a Pulmonary Consult for long-term
Azithromycin therapy for the prevention COPD exacerbations.
## Pulmonary is the only approved provider for ordering long-term Azithromycin
## therapy for COPD.
Azithromycin 250 mg po daily long-term for COPD [DI]
